newsitem.title: USA: Cooper Industries adopts holders rights plan.
newsitem.headline: Cooper Industries adopts holders rights plan.

text.p: Cooper Industries Inc said Tuesday its board adopted a shareholder rights plan with a 15 percent trigger.
Cooper said the plan is not a response to any known effort to acquire control of the company.
The company said it declared a dividend distribution of one preferred share purchase right for each share of common stock held of record on August 15.

The rights can be exercised if a person or group acquires 15 percent or more of Cooper's common stock or begins an offer for 15 percent or more of the common stock, unless the offer is on terms that are in the best interests of the company and its shareholders.

The rights would entitle the holders, other than the acquirer, to buy shares of Cooper common stock having a market value equal to two times the right's exercise price, or to buy shares of the acquiring company having a market value equal to two times the right's exercise price.

The plan provides Cooper may redeem the rights for $0.01 per right at any time before the tenth business day after a public announcement that a 15 percent position has been acquired. They expire on August 5, 2007.
